Penang light rail line gets green light, public feedback opens

By Aisyah Rahman · 30 September 2026

Share on Facebook Post on X WhatsApp

GEORGE TOWN: The federal government has approved the 29.5km Mutiara Line light rail transit project linking Komtar in George Town with Bayan Lepas on the island's southern industrial belt, ending more than a decade of debate over how the state should tackle its chronic traffic congestion. Transport officials said the approval covers the alignment, the 21 stations and the depot at Bayan Lepas, and allows land acquisition to begin early next year.

The line is expected to carry about 140,000 passengers a day when it opens, with trains every four minutes at peak hours. State executive councillor for infrastructure Zairil Khir Johari said the approval was "the single most important transport decision for Penang in a generation" and urged residents along the route to take part in the consultation that opened on Monday.

Cost and funding

The project is estimated to cost RM10.5 billion, of which the federal government will fund RM8 billion through a direct allocation spread over six years. The remaining RM2.5 billion will be raised by the state through land reclamation proceeds and a sukuk programme that the state treasury expects to price in the first half of 2027. Officials stressed that fares would be set by the federal land public transport agency and capped in line with other urban rail lines in the country.

Economists welcomed the funding split but cautioned that cost overruns on earlier rail projects in the Klang Valley ran as high as 20 per cent. "The governance framework for variations and claims will matter more than the headline number," said Dr Lim Mei Ling of the Penang Institute, who has studied the project since its first feasibility report in 2015.

Timeline

Construction is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2027 after utility relocation works, with civil works packaged into four contracts so that local contractors can bid for the smaller packages. The first trains are expected to run in 2031, and the full line is due to open by the end of 2032.

  • Land acquisition: January to December 2027
  • Utility relocation: April 2027 to March 2028
  • Civil works and stations: from the third quarter of 2027
  • Systems, trains and testing: 2029 to 2031
  • Full revenue service: by December 2032

Public feedback period

The public inspection and feedback period for the railway scheme opened on 29 September 2026 and closes on 28 November 2026 at 5pm. Printed copies of the railway scheme can be viewed at the Penang Island City Council offices at Komtar, at the Bayan Lepas district office and at public libraries along the route, while the full documents and the feedback form are available online on the railway scheme page.

Residents may submit written objections or comments by post, by email or in person at any of the three inspection centres. Each submission must state the name and address of the person making it and the section of the alignment it refers to. Officials said every submission would be answered in writing before the scheme is finalised, and that public hearings would be held in January if more than 500 objections are received.

What residents are saying

Along Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah, where the elevated track will run above the median, some shop owners worry about two years of construction noise and dust. "We support the train, but please do not close the road for months like they did elsewhere," said a hardware shop owner who has operated there since 1998. Others in the Bayan Lepas industrial zone said the line could not come soon enough: factories there employ more than 300,000 workers, most of whom commute by car or by factory bus.

"If the train gets my workers here in 30 minutes instead of 90, it pays for itself in a year." — a manufacturing plant manager in Bayan Lepas

Civil society groups have also asked for better feeder buses and safe walking routes to stations. The state government said a parallel study on feeder services and park-and-ride sites would be published for consultation in the first quarter of 2027.
